title: SUBSTITUTE: replace one piece of text

docs.syntax: =SUBSTITUTE(text,old,new,[instance]) swaps old for new everywhere, or at one instance
docs.explain:
SUBSTITUTE takes the text, the piece to look for and the piece to put in its place. It swaps every match in the string, so the call =SUBSTITUTE(A2,"-","/") turns WH-12-03 into WH/12/03. Nothing outside the match changes.

This column holds three booking references, each with two hyphens. The first screen replaces both, which is what the three-argument form does. The second adds 2 as a fourth argument, and only the second hyphen becomes a slash: WH-12/03.

The number counts occurrences of the piece you are replacing, from the left, so 2 points at the second hyphen in the string. A replace at a fixed position names a place, and breaks as soon as a reference changes length.

errors.text: The fourth argument is below 1 or is not a number, so there is no occurrence to replace.
SUBSTITUTE is misspelled, so the sheet has nothing to call.
An occurrence number past the end of the text returns the reference unchanged, and the grader sees an untouched answer.

docs.atWork: Imported codes that need a different separator before another system will read them.
docs.outcome: Replace a separator everywhere, then name a single occurrence with the fourth argument.
docs.teaches: SUBSTITUTE replacing all matches, then one named occurrence
docs.dataset: Booking references that carry two hyphens in fixed places

screens.prompt: In B2, replace every hyphen in the booking reference in A2 with a slash.

hints.syntax: =SUBSTITUTE(A2,"-","/"): the text, the piece to find, then what replaces it.
hints.func-substitute: Both hyphens move, which is what the three-argument form does with no occurrence given.
hints.require-ref: Point at A2 so every reference in the column can be checked.
hints.value: Both hyphens become slashes: WH/12/03. The digits never move.
hints.error: A piece of text that is not found leaves the string unchanged, so the grader reports a wrong answer rather than a broken formula.

reject.why: the answer is built from positions rather than from a replacement
the hyphens are removed rather than swapped
there is no underscore, so the reference comes back unchanged
the instance argument leaves the first hyphen alone
the formula reads the second reference rather than A2
the arguments fall outside the parentheses

screens.prompt: In B2, replace only the second hyphen in the booking reference in A2 with a slash.

hints.syntax: =SUBSTITUTE(A2,"-","/",2): the fourth argument is which hyphen to change.
hints.func-substitute: Only one hyphen moves, so the occurrence number has to be named.
hints.require-ref: The reference is in A2. Type it in and a corrected code never reaches the answer.
hints.value: The second hyphen turns into a slash and the first one stays: WH-12/03.
hints.error: An occurrence number past the end of the text returns the reference untouched.

reject.why: replacing a position breaks when the text changes length
without the instance argument both hyphens change
instance one replaces the first hyphen instead
there is no underscore, so nothing changes
the formula reads the second reference rather than A2
an instance number of x is not a number
the arguments fall outside the parentheses

seo.title: SUBSTITUTE in Excel: replace one piece
seo.description: SUBSTITUTE swaps a named piece of text everywhere. Add the instance argument and only the second occurrence changes, which a fixed position cannot do.
